Workspace preparation is an algorithmic server operation with a durable operation identity, explicit immutable commit basis and observed result. The service generates the owned branch and worktree path under a trusted root, records ownership and verifies common directory, branch, HEAD and project cwd before publishing readiness. Retries reconcile that exact operation and never adopt an unrelated directory. A worker inherits the plan workspace by default or requests an isolated child workspace; the server resolves and persists its actual cwd before launch. Uncommitted parent changes are not silently copied, discarded or stashed. Native children claim isolated-workspace support only when the host can actually set and attest their cwd. @status:spec/plan

Each work attempt records its plan context, actor, task and known semantic target references together with the prepared workspace and commit basis. Repeated attempts preserve assignment history. Actor identity, workspace identity and a branch name are distinct; unknown assignments stay unknown. Source and target contexts are carried through every command and navigation callback, including portfolio views. A plan's configured source and planning authority follow its own workspace rather than the project's default directory. @status:spec/plan

Integration is a durable operation bound to source and target workspace identities and exact observed commit OIDs. Prepare the integration in a separate owned worktree. The requesting plan owns the candidate and its resolution task; the target retains separate admission and write authority. Candidate, worker, graph references and diff share that one owning context even when the recorded target is the original checkout in another context. A clean merge produces a candidate for authorized review; a conflict produces a bounded resolution task in the integration worktree. Neither a clean Git merge nor a worker's report automatically accepts the semantic task. Promotion requires the accepted candidate, unchanged expected target HEAD, a clean target including protection for ignored files, and exclusive permission to write that actual target. Promote by fast-forward without overwriting ignored files. A busy target queues or refuses promotion rather than allowing competing writes. Changed target basis invalidates the preview and requires a new preparation. @status:spec/plan

Persist operation intent and state before side effects. After interruption, reconcile actual Git and workspace state with the recorded identity and commit basis before retrying. Preserve failed and conflicted artifacts for inspection. The first release does not automatically delete branches or worktrees, rewrite history, force-push, reset user changes or perform automatic stashing. Project Pause and Stop retain workspace assignments and pending integrations. Garbage collection and remote execution are separate future capabilities. @status:spec/plan

Owner addition of 2026-09-16: preserve an extension path to several people, accounts and computers communicating over a network. Human principals and memberships, provider-account references, logical agents, coordinator sessions, execution hosts and process incarnations remain distinct. Shared commands are authorized at the server, carry an accountable author, use scoped idempotency and optimistic revisions, and retain reviewer identity. Paths and provider credentials belong to a protected host binding; another client or host cannot use them merely by knowing a public object ID. Connecting another clone to an existing repository requires explicit trusted registration, not equality of remote URLs or local path strings. Current execution is local-only and refuses unsupported remote operations explicitly. A host-execution port and ownership lease/epoch contract permit later remote dispatch and fencing; the current implementation does not claim distributed locking, remote Git synchronization, account federation or multi-user authentication. Per-client selections remain separate from shared plan state. @status:spec/plan

Long-term owner vision: people may contribute their own execution hosts and model-account capacity to a shared project. Resource availability grants no authority to change the accepted project. A contribution retains submitting principal, execution host, assignment and attempt, source basis, produced artifacts and evidence origin. Execution, reporting, testing, reviewing and admission are separate authorities. A future trusted team-lead agent can coordinate review of potentially malicious contributions, but prompts and the contributor's own success reports never replace server authorization, independent checks or an explicit admission decision. Worktree separation is not a security sandbox. Execution of untrusted code will require a separately designed isolation boundary and secret policy. Credentials stay with the resource owner; capacity contribution does not pool or reveal account keys. Current local trusted execution implements none of the future public resource marketplace, hostile-code sandboxing or contributor admission services. @status:spec/plan

The future scheduling boundary separates a task's requirements from a participant's revocable resource grant and from the selected execution attempt. A grant may restrict projects, operations, model profiles, budget, concurrency and expiry; resource ownership and project authority are checked independently. Host disconnection leaves an observed or uncertain attempt, not an assumed failure or permission to replay irreversible effects. Existing scoped request identities, attempt provenance, lease epochs and separate integration admission must remain usable when a local execution port is replaced by a remote one. This is an extension constraint, not a requirement to implement a distributed scheduler in the current delivery. @status:spec/plan

All Lens clients share server-owned plan, workspace, assignment and integration data. Quick Lens supports selecting multiple plans of one project, shows the responsible actor and workspace on work items and cards, and represents fork, integration and conflict-resolution operations as stable semantic nodes and relationships. Graph distance and layout never imply elapsed time or completed integration without evidence. Events retain the full history and cross-reference the corresponding operation; notes and Trash preserve references to retired objects. @status:spec/plan

Colocated deterministic scenarios use real Git in small disposable repositories and ZapMockAgent executors. Cover two top-level plans in one repository, inherited and isolated workers, preparation before agent launch, scoped file changes, clean integration, an actual conflict and resolution, stale or dirty target refusal, restart reconciliation and graph assignment/fork/join projection. The original checkout and other contexts remain unchanged by child work. No provider inference or developer credentials are required. Mock success does not establish vendor-specific native-worktree capabilities. @status:spec/plan
Named execution catalog and task specialization

Separate the human principal, execution host, provider account/connection, agent product, model family, exact model, and named execution configuration. A configuration binds one authorized connection, model and allowed effort/context choices. Names are generated deterministically without inference, are editable, and never serve as identity. The interface presents the name first, then account/agent/provider/model/effort/context. An account label alone does not establish a different login; launches use the selected protected auth binding. @status:spec/plan

Zap Wayfinder owns a durable catalog shared by all Lens clients. The owner can add, rename, enable/disable and inspect authorized connections/configurations, allowed model choices, effort values and context presets. Browser commands refer to server-registered launch/auth bindings rather than accepting arbitrary executables, environment contents or credentials. Existing protected settings seed compatible entries; additional Codex and Claude accounts can use distinct protected auth/config homes and non-Codex profiles can use protected environment bindings. Configuration and catalog mutation require server-derived administration authority, expected revision and idempotency identity, with attributable history. Catalog reference data never enables a model/account by itself. @status:spec/plan

Task specialization is independent of ZAP WorkType, task purpose and model size tier. Initial specializations are general, architecture, backend, web_ui, testing, code_review, research, documentation, data_analysis, image_generation and automation. New task requests and work records carry the explicit specialization and requirements; titles are not used as an implicit classifier. A project can dispatch different tasks to different authorized agents/accounts/models. Existing four-tier policies and recorded selections remain compatible; the new catalog removes the four-bindings ceiling for specialized routing. @status:spec/plan

Ship editable, dated reference entries for roughly ten common model families, with exact model identifiers where verified, official source links, documented capability facts, and qualitative task-fit/economic presets. This is a curated starting point, not a measured popularity ranking or a claim of universal superiority. Owner preference gives Claude prominence for web interfaces and gpt-5.6-sol prominence as the controller for image-generation tasks when its connected execution path provides an image-generation tool. The underlying image tool model remains a separate capability and setting. Reference models that lack an installed/configured compatible execution path remain visibly unavailable. A text controller model and an image-generation tool model are distinct; an image-model identifier must never be passed as a coding CLI's conversation model. @status:spec/plan

The shared deterministic resolver first filters authorization, enabled state, actual launch binding, execution mode, required modality/tools, effort and context compatibility. It then applies editable task priorities and an economy-to-quality preference from 0 to 100, default 50. The score uses explicit heuristic suitability/economic data and explains the selected and excluded candidates; it is not a fabricated price prediction. A manual override is explicit and recorded. There is no silent upgrade to an unapproved model, account or effort. Native children retain host constraints; crossing to another agent/account is a managed dispatch only when that execution mode is allowed. @status:spec/plan

Distinguish documented maximum context, user-allowed presets, requested context, applied host configuration and actual observation. Capability states include configurable, fixed/inherited, unsupported and unknown. Presets must fit both model and adapter limits. A budget or compaction setting does not enlarge a model's context window. Unsupported arbitrary context/effort overrides are refused or shown as provider-controlled before launch, never silently ignored. Codex's documented model_context_window is a host configuration limit; Claude long-context model variants and other provider settings require their own evidence. @status:spec/plan

Catalog settings include a remaining-subscription deprioritization toggle and configurable percentage threshold, initially 10 percent when enabled. Fresh applicable quota observations below the threshold lower priority without revoking permission or silently changing a running selection. Usage snapshots retain account binding, provider/bucket identity, units, window/reset time, source and observation time. Exact remaining tokens are displayed only when the source actually supplies them; percentages, token consumption and API credit balances are different quantities. Unknown, unsupported and stale observations remain explicit, not zero. Codex uses its authenticated account/rateLimits/read interface, preferring the multi-bucket result; no earned reset, purchase or notification is performed. Quota refresh is read-only, bounded and rate-limited, with no model polling. Selected bucket applicability is explicit rather than guessed from labels. Freshness defaults to five minutes, configurable by trusted service policy. @status:spec/plan

Selections record catalog/routing revision, specialization, friendly configuration name, account/launch binding, actual agent/model, requested and applied effort/context, ranking explanation and relevant usage basis. Shared preview and actual dispatch use the same resolver. Changing preferences affects new selections; existing runs retain their exact assignment. Disabling a configuration/connection prevents new dispatch through it, including a new process resume, while preserving history and existing files. It does not silently migrate an active conversation to another account or model. Account, cwd/worktree, model and control epoch remain independent identities. @status:spec/plan

ZapMock may advertise synthetic personas representing different model families, accounts, capabilities, context limits and quota windows, while the actual provider remains zap_mock and all evidence remains explicitly synthetic. A trusted test host may explicitly register a synthetic binding with no credential, home or environment authority; ordinary account discovery never creates one. Its process continues to run zap-mock/deterministic-v1, independently of emulated model metadata. Colocated replayable scenarios exercise the real catalog store/service/resolver and recording or mock-process dispatch: ten-family choices, two accounts of one provider, task routing, slider endpoints, low/fresh versus stale/unknown quota, capability refusal, renaming, revocation, CAS/replay, restart, project isolation and pinned existing selections. They do not read real credentials or call models. @status:spec/plan

Implement the catalog, shared routing/dispatch integration and usable admin UI before spending live model tokens. Validate the actual browser UI and current deterministic corpus. Then use one tiny authorized GPT configuration and one tiny Claude configuration to check real selection/launch propagation, with a tiny project boot and no comparative model-quality campaign. Account/quota and protocol handshakes may be checked without inference. Preserve durable recovery notes throughout. Ten new proprietary agent drivers, full account-billing administration, remote multi-user federation and speculative exhaustive edge testing are outside this slice. @status:spec/plan
Source installation through VibeVM

A source bootstrap creates a dedicated, explicitly marked Vibe consumer workspace under the selected user's settings root, normally ~/.vibe/opt/apps/zap. It installs the pinned Zap packages from an explicit local source registry through ordinary Vibe materialisation. The runtime must not depend on the original checkout after installation. Installation files are distinct from ~/.vibe/zap project state and provider account homes. @status:spec/plan

The dedicated installer host owns the phase:build script and the package:static-file plus deploy:vibe-opt-launcher declarations. A dependency on Lens in an ordinary project must not activate its application installer. The build runs locked npm installation and the existing Node/browser/Electron build in the materialised Lens slot, and can build the existing Rust zap binary through Vibe's declared-binary dispatch. No install hook publishes user launchers; only the explicit deploy profile does so with Vibe receipts. @status:spec/plan

Launchers address an immutable generated runtime payload retained inside the installer workspace, rather than the mutable development checkout or mutable build output. The generation binds source/package inputs, platform and relevant runtime identity. Preparation of a new generation does not replace files used by an existing process. Old generated payloads are retained as build cache; Vibe receipts own published launchers, not that entire cache. Successful deployment is required before reporting an installation as ready. @status:spec/plan

The source bootstrap provides install, update, status and uninstall operations, with an explicit settings-directory override for isolation and a local registry override. Help/status do not start agents. Node 24 and npm are build prerequisites; Rust/Cargo is required when installing the engine. The default installation includes Lens and the engine; an explicit Lens-only option may omit Rust. No model calls or binary-release publication form part of installation. Standard dependency downloads remain distinct from downloading a Zap binary release. @status:spec/plan

The bootstrap refuses unrelated or unmarked installation directories, executes programs with structured arguments, and confines temporary deletion or movement to verified installation-owned paths. Vibe deployment refuses unowned or modified launchers. Uninstall first invokes receipt-owned undeploy and preserves application/user state, account credentials and retained installation cache. PATH and machine-wide settings are not silently changed. A failed build or deploy cannot be labelled success or replace an already usable runtime generation silently. @status:spec/plan

Colocated deterministic tests and a registered mock scenario cover bootstrap command construction, ownership refusal, paths with spaces, update/failure boundaries and data preservation. Root acceptance runs actual Vibe source materialisation, build, package and deploy under an isolated settings root, executes installed help and a browser startup without inference, verifies update/undeploy receipts, and demonstrates launch independence from the original checkout. Use the existing package gates without a new live model test. @status:spec/plan
Short native installation and command entry points

The normal source installation is vibe install -g org.vibevm.zap/zap, using the generic user-application dispatcher in spec://org.vibevm.core/vibevm/common/PROP-059#root. Update and uninstall use the same coordinate with their native -g verbs. The advanced Node bootstrap remains available but is not the primary user path. @status:impl/done

The provider entry tooling/source-install/application.mjs validates the generic context, exact Zap/Lens identities, settings/host binding and operation, then invokes the accepted source bootstrap with structured options and the current native Vibe executable. It writes a matching generic reply only after actual success, returns its management entry from a retained immutable runtime generation, and reports the exact absolute destination and SHA-256 of every receipt-owned public source launcher so a later binary transition can replace or restore those bytes transactionally. No new model call, user credential copy or extra project mutation is introduced. @status:impl/done

zap-quicklens uses the ordinary product launcher. zap-server uses the same state, owner, services and HTTP presentation but forcibly disables browser/Electron opening; starting either command does not start agent work. Help returns before state creation or provider discovery. The old zap-quick-lens and advanced zap-wayfinder spellings retain compatibility. All launchers remain declared package bins and receipt-owned Vibe deployments. @status:impl/done

The Zap source manifest names only the stable external distribution-index locator. The release-side index binds each platform artifact URL, size and digest to its exact application identity, immutable source commit and Vibe portable source-tree hash; those artifact facts never enter the source commit they describe. A Windows x64 ZIP carries bundled Node.js 24, production Lens dependencies including Electron and node-pty, Rust Zap, actual license notices, stable public launchers and one generation-relative management launcher. Its root descriptor lists every regular ZIP entry except itself with exact size and SHA-256, rejects links, traversal and case collisions, and binds the verified source commit and `sha256-tree/1` checkout. Public launcher bytes copied to the settings bin directory delegate through Vibe's stable management shim to the selected immutable generation, so spaces and a clean host PATH are supported without embedding an asset hash. Vibe core owns binary preference, index/ZIP verification, publication receipts and source fallback; an unsupported platform or explicitly selected source route uses the separately verified source application and ordinary registries. Builder source and deterministic fixtures are implementation candidates until an actual committed native bundle passes core cross-verification and release acceptance. @status:spec/done

Colocated deterministic tests and simulation cover the adapter and short/headless command behavior. Root acceptance exercises the actual generic native command, installed short launchers and original-source-independent uninstall in an isolated user settings directory, without LLM inference. @status:impl/done
